contentObjective: I can recognize when two quantities change together, and identify which one is the independent variable and which is the dependent variable.

steps: 1. Independent Variable (x): The input / cause that is chosen or changes freely
2. Dependent Variable (y): The output / effect that depends on the independent variable

revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Selling Pizzas
revealWordProblem.text:
At a local pizza shop, a customer can order a large pizza with up to three different toppings for $12.49. The shop is open daily from 11 a.m. to 9 p.m. and has a total of 6 employees. The shop spends $1.15 on cheese and $1.95 on sauce for each pizza.
Question: How would you describe the relationship between the number of large pizzas sold and each of the following: the hours the shop is open, the number of employees who work in the shop, the cost of cheese each week, and the cost of sauce each week?
revealWordProblem.imageAlt: A pizzeria sign showing hours of 11 a.m. to 9 p.m. and a large pizza with up to 3 toppings for $12.49.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: Sort each pair by whether one quantity depends on the other. The hours the shop is open do not change when more pizzas sell — the shop is open 11 to 9 either way — so the hours are independent of pizza sales. The number of employees is also independent day to day; 6 people work whether the shop sells 40 pizzas or 90. Cheese cost does depend on pizzas sold: every pizza uses $1.15 of cheese, so weekly cheese cost = 1.15p, where p is the number of pizzas. Sauce works the same way at $1.95 a pizza, so weekly sauce cost = 1.95p. In both of those, p is the independent variable and the cost is the dependent variable, and each cost grows at a steady rate as p grows.

questions.stem: Akela chooses how many hours of sunlight each tray gets. Which is the INDEPENDENT variable?
questions.explanation: Akela chooses the sunlight, so sunlight is subject to choice — that makes it independent.
choiceFeedback: You have the two variables backward. Ask which one someone gets to CHOOSE — that one is independent.
The number of trays is not one of the two quantities being related here.
The number of seeds is not one of the two quantities being related here.
hints: Which quantity did Akela get to decide?
Sunlight was set by where she put the tray.
The one subject to choice is independent.
questions.stemEs: Akela escoge cuántas horas de luz solar recibe cada bandeja. ¿Cuál es la variable INDEPENDIENTE?
questions.explanationEs: Akela escoge la luz solar, así que la luz solar es lo que se escoge — eso la hace independiente.
hintsEs: ¿Cuál cantidad pudo decidir Akela?
La luz solar la determinó dónde puso la bandeja.
La que se escoge es la independiente.

questions.stem: In Akela's experiment, which is the DEPENDENT variable?
questions.explanation: Height responds to how much sunlight the tray received, so height is the dependent variable.
choiceFeedback: You have the two variables backward. Ask which one someone gets to CHOOSE — that one is independent.
The kind of seed was the same for all three trays.
The tray size was the same for all three trays.
hints: Which quantity RESPONDED to the other?
Akela did not choose how tall the plants grew.
The responding quantity is dependent.
questions.stemEs: En el experimento de Akela, ¿cuál es la variable DEPENDIENTE?
questions.explanationEs: La altura responde a cuánta luz solar recibió la bandeja, así que la altura es la variable dependiente.
hintsEs: ¿Cuál cantidad RESPONDIÓ a la otra?
Akela no escogió qué tan alto crecieron las plantas.
La cantidad que responde es la dependiente.

questions.stem: Claire burned 123 Calories on a 30-minute jog. Which quantity is subject to choice?
questions.explanation: Claire decides how long to jog. The Calories follow from that decision.
choiceFeedback: You have the two variables backward. Ask which one someone gets to CHOOSE — that one is independent.
Heart rate is not one of the two quantities in this problem.
The weather is not one of the two quantities in this problem.
hints: What does Claire decide before she starts?
She sets the time on the tracker.
Calories are the result, not the choice.
questions.stemEs: Claire quemó 123 calorías en un trote de 30 minutos. ¿Cuál cantidad es la que se escoge?
questions.explanationEs: Claire decide cuánto tiempo trotar. Las calorías dependen de esa decisión.
hintsEs: ¿Qué decide Claire antes de empezar?
Ella fija el tiempo en el reloj.
Las calorías son el resultado, no la decisión.

level1.stem: Movie tickets cost $2 each. The table pairs tickets bought (x) with total cost (y). Complete the table, then name the variable that DEPENDS on the other — type cost or tickets.

steps.prompt: The total changes BECAUSE the tickets change, so the dependent variable is the ___ (type cost or tickets).
steps.promptEs: El total cambia PORQUE cambian los boletos, así que la variable dependiente es ___ (escribe cost o tickets).

hints: Re-read the question. What exactly is it asking you to find?
Ask which quantity you choose first, and which one is decided FOR you by that choice.
Start like this: Cost of 2 tickets: 2 × 2 = 4.
level1.explanation: Cost of 2 tickets: 2 × 2 = 4. Cost of 3 tickets: 3 × 2 = 6. The total changes BECAUSE the tickets change, so the dependent variable is the cost (type cost or tickets).
level1.stemEs: Cada boleto de cine cuesta $2. La tabla empareja boletos comprados (x) con el costo total (y). Completa la tabla y nombra la variable que DEPENDE de la otra — escribe cost (costo) o tickets (boletos).
hintsEs: Vuelve a leer la pregunta. ¿Qué te pide encontrar exactamente?
Pregunta qué cantidad eliges primero y cuál queda decidida POR esa elección.
Empieza así: Costo de 2 boletos: 2 × 2 = 4.
level1.explanationEs: Costo de 2 boletos: 2 × 2 = 4. Costo de 3 boletos: 3 × 2 = 6. El total cambia PORQUE cambian los boletos, así que la variable dependiente es cost (escribe cost o tickets).

level1.stem: Which sentence is written in the correct order?
choices: Minutes jogged depends on Calories burned.
Calories burned depends on Calories burned.
Neither quantity depends on the other.
Calories burned depends on minutes jogged.
level1.explanation: The dependent quantity comes first in the sentence '___ depends on ___ .' Calories respond to time, so Calories depend on minutes.
choiceFeedback: You have the two variables backward. Ask which one someone gets to CHOOSE — that one is independent.
A quantity cannot depend on itself.
These two quantities are clearly related — more time means more Calories.
hints: Say both versions out loud. Which one is true?
Claire chooses the minutes.
The responder goes first: 'responder depends on chooser.'
level1.stemEs: ¿Cuál oración está escrita en el orden correcto?
level1.explanationEs: La cantidad dependiente va primero en la oración '___ depende de ___ .' Las calorías responden al tiempo, así que las calorías dependen de los minutos.
hintsEs: Di en voz alta las dos versiones. ¿Cuál es verdadera?
Claire escoge los minutos.
El que responde va primero: 'el que responde depende del que escoge'.

level2.stem: Claire jogs 30 minutes and burns 123 Calories. At the same rate, how many Calories would a 90-minute jog burn?
level2.explanation: 30 minutes burned 123 Calories, and 90 is 3 times 30, so the Calories are 3 times 123, which is 369.
choiceFeedback: 246 Calories is the 60-minute jog, not the 90-minute jog.
That is a rounded guess — scale 123 by the same factor as the time.
That is not the result of tripling 123.
hints: How many times longer is 90 minutes than 30 minutes?
90 divided by 30 is 3.
Multiply 123 by 3.
level2.stemEs: Claire trota 30 minutos y quema 123 calorías. A la misma tasa, ¿cuántas calorías quemaría un trote de 90 minutos?
level2.explanationEs: 30 minutos quemaron 123 calorías, y 90 es 3 veces 30, así que las calorías son 3 veces 123, o sea 369.
hintsEs: ¿Cuántas veces más largo es 90 minutos que 30 minutos?
90 dividido entre 30 es 3.
Multiplica 123 por 3.

level2.stem: Which of these pairs is NOT a dependent relationship?
choices: Number of pizzas sold and weekly cost of cheese
Number of pizzas sold and number of employees the shop has
level2.explanation: The shop has 6 employees whether it sells 5 pizzas or 500. That count does not respond to pizza sales.
choiceFeedback: Cheese cost DOES rise with more pizzas, so this pair is related.
Calories DO rise with more jogging, so this pair is related.
Cost DOES rise with more tickets, so this pair is related.
hints: Which one stays the same no matter what?
The staff list does not change when a pizza is sold.
Look for the pair that does not move together.
level2.stemEs: ¿Cuál de estos pares NO es una relación de dependencia?

La lista de empleados no cambia cuando se vende una pizza.
Busca el par que no cambia junto.

level3.stem: Devon adds a different number of scoops of plant food to each tray of seedlings. Two weeks later he counts the new leaves on every tray. Which pair correctly names the variables?
choices: Independent: new leaves counted; Dependent: scoops of plant food
Independent: scoops of plant food; Dependent: new leaves counted
Independent: the number of trays; Dependent: scoops of plant food
Independent: new leaves counted; Dependent: the two weeks of growing time
choiceFeedback: These are reversed. Devon chooses how many scoops a tray gets, and the leaves respond.
The trays are only containers. What Devon varies on purpose is the scoops of plant food.
The two weeks are the same for every tray, so nothing there varies. Devon sets the scoops.
level3.explanation: Devon chooses how many scoops of plant food a tray receives, so the scoops are subject to choice and are the independent variable. The new leaves respond to that choice, so the leaf count is the dependent variable. The sentence check works only one way: the number of new leaves depends on the scoops of plant food.

level3.stem: Two quantities are related. Which statement is ALWAYS true?
choices: The independent variable is always the larger number
The independent variable is subject to choice
The dependent variable is always measured in dollars
The independent variable is always listed first in a table
level3.explanation: Being subject to choice is the definition. Size, units, and table position are not part of it.
choiceFeedback: A choice can be a small number — 1 hour is independent just as much as 100 hours.
Dependent variables can be centimeters, Calories, miles — anything that responds.
Table layout is a convention, not a definition.
hints: Which option restates the definition?
Definitions do not depend on size or units.
Choice is the deciding test.
level3.stemEs: Dos cantidades están relacionadas. ¿Cuál enunciado es SIEMPRE verdadero?
level3.explanationEs: Ser lo que uno escoge es la definición. El tamaño, las unidades y la posición en la tabla no forman parte de ella.
hintsEs: ¿Cuál opción repite la definición?
Las definiciones no dependen del tamaño ni de las unidades.
Lo que se escoge es la prueba decisiva.

level3.stem: Give an example where the SAME quantity can be independent in one problem and dependent in another.
choices: Time: chosen when you pick how long to jog, but measured as a result when you run a set distance
A quantity can never switch roles
level3.explanation: Claire's two problems show exactly this: minutes is a choice in one and a result in the other.
choiceFeedback: Compare Claire's two jogs — in the 3-mile version time is the result.
In the 30-minute jog Claire chose the time, so it was independent there.
The role depends on the problem, not on the quantity itself.
hints: Look back at Claire's two problems.
In one she set minutes; in the other she set miles.
The role depends on what was chosen.
level3.stemEs: Da un ejemplo donde la MISMA cantidad pueda ser independiente en un problema y dependiente en otro.
level3.explanationEs: Los dos problemas de Claire muestran exactamente esto: los minutos son una decisión en uno y un resultado en el otro.
hintsEs: Vuelve a mirar los dos problemas de Claire.
En uno ella fijó los minutos; en el otro fijó las millas.
El papel depende de lo que se escogió.
